question:
A bounded feasible region of a linear programming problem has corner points $O(0,0)$, $A(6,0)$, $B(6,2)$, $C(2,6)$ and $D(0,6)$. The objective function is $Z=2x+2y$. Using the corner point method:
(i) Find the maximum value of $Z$.
(ii) Examine whether the maximum solution is unique. Justify your answer.
explanation:
Step 1: Evaluating the objective function at the corner points
Using $Z=2x+2y$, we obtain $$Z_O=0,\quad Z_A=12,\quad Z_B=16,\quad Z_C=16,\quad Z_D=12$$
Step 2: Determining the maximum value
The largest value is $16$, and it occurs at both $B(6,2)$ and $C(2,6)$. Hence, the maximum value is $$Z_{\max}=16$$
Step 3: Examining uniqueness
Since two distinct corner points give the same maximum value, the optimal solution is not unique.
Step 4: Using the multiple-optimum result
Whenever two corner points give the same optimal value, every point on the line segment joining them also gives that optimal value.
Step 5: Conclusion
Therefore, every point on the segment joining $B(6,2)$ and $C(2,6)$ is an optimal solution, and all such points give the maximum value $16$.

options.A:
(i) Maximum value $16$
(ii) The solution is unique at $B(6,2)$
options.B:
(i) Maximum value $16$
(ii) The solution is not unique; every point on segment $BC$ is optimal
options.C:
(i) Maximum value $12$
(ii) The solution is not unique; $A$ and $D$ are optimal
options.D:
(i) Maximum value $20$
(ii) The solution is unique at $C(2,6)$
